source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament (with some Hebrews + Pauline epistles lacunae); complete Matthew
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: No early-papyrus witness preserves Matthew 7 within the 2nd-3rd c. CE corpus for these target verses; primary witnesses are the 4th c. uncials Vaticanus + Sinaiticus.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference (where variants are documented)
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c. CE). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments (4th c. CE). Davies-Allison ICC 1988-1997; Luz Hermeneia 2001-2007; France NICNT 2007; Hagner WBC 1993-1995; Nolland NIGTC 2005; Betz Hermeneia 1995; Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials.

verses.text: Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε·
verses.translit: Mē krinete, hina mē krithēte·
verses.notes: JUDGMENT-PROHIBITION OPENING. *krinō* — judge / discern / condemn. The Matthean form is unqualified; the Lukan parallel (Lk 6:37) expands. Often misread as a blanket discernment-prohibition; the surrounding context (vv.6, 15-20) shows discernment IS required — the prohibition targets condemnatory judgment specifically. Davies-Allison ICC 1.667-669.

verses.text: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε, καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: en hō gar krimati krinete krithēsesthe, kai en hō metrō metreite metrēthēsetai hymin.
verses.notes: MEASURE-FOR-MEASURE PRINCIPLE. Direct rabbinic parallel: *middâ kěneged middâ* (m. Sotah 1:7; b. Sanhedrin 100a). The principle is widespread in 1st-c. Jewish ethics. Cross-corpus: cf. Mk 4:24; Lk 6:38; cf. Ps Sol 5:14.

verses.text: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς;
verses.translit: ti de blepeis to karphos to en tō ophthalmō tou adelphou sou, tēn de en tō sō ophthalmō dokon ou katanoeis?
verses.notes: SPECK-AND-LOG HYPERBOLE. *karphos* (dry twig, splinter) vs *dokos* (load-bearing roof beam). The deliberately-absurd disproportion is rhetorical. cf. b. Bava Batra 15b (rabbinic parallel: 'take the splinter from between your teeth').

verses.text: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ;
verses.translit: ē pōs ereis tō adelphō sou· Aphes ekbalō to karphos ek tou ophthalmou sou, kai idou hē dokos en tō ophthalmō sou?
verses.notes: Continuation of the speck-log image. *aphes* ("let me") + subjunctive *ekbalō* — a courteous request-construction.

verses.text: ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
verses.translit: hypokrita, ekbale prōton ek tou ophthalmou sou tēn dokon, kai tote diablepseis ekbalein to karphos ek tou ophthalmou tou adelphou sou.
verses.notes: Self-correction-before-other-correction. *diablepseis* (you will see-through-clearly) — improved vision after log-removal. NOT a blanket prohibition of correction but a sequencing rule.

verses.text: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, μήποτε καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: Mē dōte to hagion tois kysin, mēde balēte tous margaritas hymōn emprosthen tōn choirōn, mēpote katapatēsousin autous en tois posin autōn kai straphentes rhēxōsin hymas.
verses.notes: DOGS-AND-SWINE saying. Dogs + swine = the two paradigmatic-unclean animals in Jewish thought. The image of pearls trampled by swine + dogs returning to attack is hyperbolic. Some early Christian writers (Didache 9:5) cite this as restricting Eucharist to the baptized. **EDITOR FLAG**: the verse should NOT be translated as ethnic/anti-Gentile slur (some pre-modern readings); the metaphor is type-specific (those incapable of receiving holy things), not ethnic. Davies-Allison ICC 1.675-681.

verses.text: Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: Aiteite, kai dothēsetai hymin· zēteite, kai heurēsete· krouete, kai anoigēsetai hymin.
verses.notes: ASK-SEEK-KNOCK TRIAD. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: Raël *The Role of Christ* engages vv.7-11 as 'the Elohim-relationship pattern.' **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve text; do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian Elohim-prayer-receptivity reading. The three present-imperatives (*aiteite, zēteite, krouete*) imply continuous action. The three passives (*dothēsetai, heurēsete-active, anoigēsetai*) are divine passives. Davies-Allison ICC 1.681-684.

verses.text: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
verses.translit: pas gar ho aitōn lambanei kai ho zētōn heuriskei kai tō krouonti anoigēsetai.
verses.notes: Generalization of v.7 — present-active forms make the principle universal. *pas* (every) — no qualifier on who receives.

verses.text: ἢ τίς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος, ὃν αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον — μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
verses.translit: ē tis estin ex hymōn anthrōpos, hon aitēsei ho huios autou arton — mē lithon epidōsei autō?
verses.notes: FATHER-AND-SON ANALOGY. Bread / stone — visually similar (Galilean limestone vs limestone-pebble-loaves). The rhetorical question expects 'no.'

verses.text: ἢ καὶ ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει — μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
verses.translit: ē kai ichthyn aitēsei — mē ophin epidōsei autō?
verses.notes: Second analogy — fish / snake. Visually similar (eel-like fish vs water-snake). Both v.9 and v.10 set up the *qal vāḥōmer* of v.11.

verses.text: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: ei oun hymeis ponēroi ontes oidate domata agatha didonai tois teknois hymōn, posō mallon ho patēr hymōn ho en tois ouranois dōsei agatha tois aitousin auton.
verses.notes: QAL VĀḤŌMER — if you (limited, evil) give good gifts, how much more the heavenly Father. *ponēroi ontes* (being evil) — assumes human depravity as baseline. Lukan parallel (Lk 11:13) reads *pneuma hagion* (Holy Spirit) where Matthew has *agatha* (good things) — the Matthean reading is more general.

verses.text: Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
verses.translit: Panta oun hosa ean thelēte hina poiōsin hymin hoi anthrōpoi, houtōs kai hymeis poieite autois· houtos gar estin ho nomos kai hoi prophētai.
verses.notes: GOLDEN RULE. The positive form distinctive to the Jesus-tradition (cf. Lk 6:31); the negative form ("do not do what you would not want done") is widely attested in Hellenistic + Jewish + early-Christian sources (Tob 4:15; Hillel in b. Shabbat 31a; Did 1:2; cf. Confucius *Analects* 15:24). The summary-formula *ho nomos kai hoi prophētai* explicitly frames the golden rule as Torah-summary (parallel to Mt 22:40). Davies-Allison ICC 1.685-688.

verses.text: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης· ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν, καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι δι' αὐτῆς·
verses.translit: Eiselthate dia tēs stenēs pylēs· hoti plateia hē pylē kai eurychōros hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn apōleian, kai polloi eisin hoi eiserchomenoi di' autēs·
verses.notes: NARROW GATE. The two-ways topos — widely attested: Deut 30:15-19; Ps 1; Jer 21:8; Prov 4:18-19; *Did* 1-6; *Barn* 18-20; 1QS 3-4 (Qumran two-spirits doctrine); cf. Hesiod *Works and Days* 287-292 (the two paths of virtue and vice). Davies-Allison ICC 1.696-700.

verses.text: τί στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν.
verses.translit: ti stenē hē pylē kai tethlimmenē hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn zōēn, kai oligoi eisin hoi heuriskontes autēn.
verses.notes: Variant: NA28/SBLGNT/Vaticanus read *ti* ("how!" — exclamatory); some witnesses read *hoti* ("because"). The exclamatory reading is preferred. *zōē* (life) = eschatological life — standard Jewish-apocalyptic usage.

verses.text: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν, οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων, ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες.
verses.translit: Prosechete apo tōn pseudoprophētōn, hoitines erchontai pros hymas en endymasi probatōn, esōthen de eisin lykoi harpages.
verses.notes: WOLVES-IN-SHEEP'S-CLOTHING. *pseudoprophētēs* — pseudo-prophet, false prophet. The wolf-sheep image: cf. Ezek 22:27; Zeph 3:3; cf. Mt 10:16 (disciples sent as sheep among wolves). The verse pre-supposes a community-context where prophetic-figures circulate (cf. Mt 24:11, 24).

verses.text: ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς· μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα;
verses.translit: apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous· mēti syllegousin apo akanthōn staphylas ē apo tribolōn syka?
verses.notes: FRUIT-TEST PRINCIPLE. The discernment-criterion is character/effect, not credential. Thorn-bushes (*akanthai*) and thistles (*triboloi*) yield no grapes / figs. cf. James 3:12.

verses.text: οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ, τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ·
verses.translit: houtōs pan dendron agathon karpous kalous poiei, to de sapron dendron karpous ponērous poiei·
verses.notes: Good-tree / bad-tree generalization. *sapros* (rotten, putrid) — strong term. Echoes Jer 17:7-10.

verses.text: οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖν, οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν.
verses.translit: ou dynatai dendron agathon karpous ponērous poiein, oude dendron sapron karpous kalous poiein.
verses.notes: Absolute impossibility of cross-fruit-bearing. Strong statement of nature-determined-action; in tension with Pauline anthropology of transformation; in keeping with Matthean ethical determinism (cf. 12:33-37).

verses.text: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
verses.translit: pan dendron mē poioun karpon kalon ekkoptetai kai eis pyr balletai.
verses.notes: Echoes John the Baptist's preaching (Mt 3:10) — verbatim repetition. The redactor links Jesus's teaching to the Baptist's eschatological-axe imagery.

verses.text: ἄρα γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.
verses.translit: ara ge apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous.
verses.notes: Restatement / inclusio with v.16 closing the unit.

verses.text: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε, εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ' ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
verses.translit: Ou pas ho legōn moi· Kyrie kyrie, eiseleusetai eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn, all' ho poiōn to thelēma tou patros mou tou en tois ouranois.
verses.notes: LORD-LORD SAYING. *Kyrios* address — confession-not-sufficient principle. Note the speaker's self-reference *tou patros mou* (MY Father) — distinguishing Jesus's filial relationship from disciples' (*patēr hymōn*); a high Christological note within the Sermon.

verses.text: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· Κύριε κύριε, οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν;
verses.translit: polloi erousin moi en ekeinē tē hēmera· Kyrie kyrie, ou tō sō onomati eprophēteusamen, kai tō sō onomati daimonia exebalomen, kai tō sō onomati dynameis pollas epoiēsamen?
verses.notes: *en ekeinē tē hēmera* — that day = day of judgment. Charismatic activities (prophecy, exorcism, miracles) in Jesus's name not sufficient. The verse pre-supposes a Matthean-community context where such activities are claimed (cf. Mt 24:24).

verses.text: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν.
verses.translit: kai tote homologēsō autois hoti Oudepote egnōn hymas· apochōreite ap' emou hoi ergazomenoi tēn anomian.
verses.notes: *oudepote egnōn hymas* ("I never knew you") — relational knowledge, not informational. Citation of Ps 6:9 LXX (*apostēte ap' emou pantes hoi ergazomenoi tēn anomian*). *anomia* — lawlessness; for Matthew this means Torah-non-observance (Mt 5:17-20 frame), in tension with Pauline *anomia* = sin generally.

verses.text: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς, ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
verses.translit: Pas oun hostis akouei mou tous logous toutous kai poiei autous, homoiōthēsetai andri phronimō, hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn petran.
verses.notes: WISE-BUILDER. *phronimos* (prudent, sensible) — Matthean keyword (10:16; 24:45; 25:2-9). The hearing+doing combination (echoed in Jas 1:22-25). *petra* (bedrock) vs *ammos* (sand) — Palestinian flash-flood geology.

verses.text: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν, τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
verses.translit: kai katebē hē brochē kai ēlthon hoi potamoi kai epneusan hoi anemoi kai prosepesan tē oikia ekeinē, kai ouk epesen, tethemeliōto gar epi tēn petran.
verses.notes: Triple-storm description — rain, rivers, winds. *tethemeliōto* (pluperfect — 'had-been-founded') — emphasizes the prior-action of solid foundation.

verses.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον.
verses.translit: kai pas ho akouōn mou tous logous toutous kai mē poiōn autous homoiōthēsetai andri mōrō, hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn ammon.
verses.notes: FOOLISH-BUILDER. *mōros* (foolish) — recall the same word at Mt 5:22 forbidden as insult; here used as wisdom-tradition typological label. Sand = the dry-season wadi-bed, deceptively flat and accessible until the rains.

verses.text: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.
verses.translit: kai katebē hē brochē kai ēlthon hoi potamoi kai epneusan hoi anemoi kai prosekopsan tē oikia ekeinē, kai epesen, kai ēn hē ptōsis autēs megalē.
verses.notes: Note slight verb variation between v.25 (*prosepesan* — fell against) and v.27 (*prosekopsan* — struck against) — possibly Matthean rhetorical variation. *hē ptōsis autēs megalē* — 'great was its fall' — the dramatic closing image of the entire Sermon.

verses.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tous logous toutous, exeplēssonto hoi ochloi epi tē didachē autou·
verses.notes: STRUCTURAL CLOSE OF DISCOURSE 1. *kai egeneto hote etelesen* — the Matthean discourse-closing formula, recurring at 11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1 — marking the five major discourses (the Mosaic-pentateuchal structure of Matthew). *exeplēssonto* — they were astounded. cf. Allison *The New Moses* 1993.

verses.text: ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: ēn gar didaskōn autous hōs exousian echōn kai ouch hōs hoi grammateis autōn.
verses.notes: AUTHORITY-CONTRAST. *exousia* (authority) vs the *grammateis* (scribes) — the scribes taught from citation/tradition; the Sermon's six-fold *egō de legō hymin* (Mt 5:22, 28, 32, 34, 39, 44) is the direct-authority claim. Variant: *autōn* (their scribes — Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, NA28); some MSS read without *autōn* or with addition *kai hoi Pharisaioi*.
